clue.text: Diversion gives an essential cover for English soldiers

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped around the others like a cover laid over them

parts.note: an essential thing is a must, so 'an essential' is A MUST
soldiers are men, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A diversion supplies something soldiers from England cannot do without for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover for' puts E MEN inside A MUST, splitting it as A MUS...T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that diverts or entertains you is an amusement, a pastime.

clue.text: Liberal politician gets in the beer

indicators.note: the politician gets in among the beer, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ale is beer
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A Liberal Party politician turns up at the pub for a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, which is synonymous with abundant.

clue.text: Wild pursuer of regal status

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A ruthless claimant chases after the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer too: someone wildly pursuing royal rank is a throne-grabber.
explanation.definitionFit: One who seizes a throne without right is wildly pursuing regal status.

clue.text: A keyhole operation?

parts.note: E is a musical key
a vent is a hole for air to escape

explanation.surface: A question about keyhole surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests keyhole surgery; instead split 'keyhole' into key and hole.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation, such as a military action, is an occurrence or happening.

clue.text: Say, that's quick!

definitions.meaning: to say is to put into words, to voice
fast, as of a train that makes few stops

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on how fast something was.
explanation.definitionFit: To express is to say something; an express train or delivery is a quick one.

clue.text: Trial run of stroke on river

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece comes after, resting on, the other

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England, famed for trout
a drive is a stroke in golf or cricket

explanation.surface: Testing a new rowing stroke out on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a chalk-stream river in southern England, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying out a car before buying is a trial run of the vehicle.

clue.text: The advantage being sharp gives one

definitions.meaning: an advantage or lead over others
a sharp blade has a keen cutting rim

explanation.surface: Quick wit is said to put you ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge means holding an advantage; a blade that is sharp has a keen cutting side.

clue.text: Demand observance in French Foreign Legion, say

parts.note: en is French for in
the French Foreign Legion is an example of a fighting force

explanation.surface: Discipline is imposed in the French Foreign Legion.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand that a law or rule be observed is to compel compliance with it.

clue.text: See post go out in March

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Watching a sentry leave his post in the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month; it is the verb or noun for a stiff military walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff-legged parade march, used by some armies, is a particular style of marching.

clue.text: Having erected the Christmas tree, make things tidy

definitions.meaning: a spruce is the usual Christmas tree; once erected it is up

explanation.surface: Putting up the tree and then tidying the house at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas spruce standing upright is a spruce up; to smarten is to tidy.

clue.text: Feeling affection for someone, was somewhat lenient

definitions.meaning: being sweet on, fond of, someone

explanation.surface: A fondness for someone made a person go easy on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sweet on someone and being lenient towards them are both expressed by this phrasal idiom.

clue.text: Catch sight of former wife going in, an erotically exciting woman

indicators.note: the former wife goes inside the other word

parts.note: to spot is to catch sight of
an ex is a former wife

explanation.surface: Someone glimpses their ex-wife entering with an alluring woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman regarded as sexually alluring is colloquially called this.

clue.text: Perhaps Ned does right to get confirmed

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Ned behaves properly and so gets confirmed in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged pool is NEDDOES plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A confirmed decision is one that has been approved or ratified.

clue.text: Batsman who hits five fours?

parts.note: five fours make twenty, a score, so one who hits that many is a maker of runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer strikes five boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty; in cricket a four is a boundary hit, so five fours is twenty runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who makes runs scores them, and twenty is a score.

clue.text: Aplomb of company representative certain about nothing

indicators.note: certain is placed about, next to, the nothing

parts.note: an MP is an elected representative
O is zero, nothing
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A firm's representative keeps calm, sure of everything except nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance and calmness under pressure.

clue.text: Restore control to the country

parts.note: a rein controls a horse; to rein is to control
a state is a country

explanation.surface: Restoring control of the nation to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to office is to put them back in their former position.

clue.text: Lets it break to a point that could be lethal

definitions.text: a point that could be lethal

indicators.note: breaking the words lets their letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Breaking through to a sharp point could prove deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagger with a narrow sharp blade has a deadly point.

clue.text: Breaking up may be wonderful

explanation.surface: A breakup might turn out to be marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering things and something excellent are both called by this word, the second as British slang.

clue.text: Making speed on foot

indicators.note: making the letters into something new rearranges them

explanation.surface: Hurrying along on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' seems to be a walker's; it is a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of two long syllables is a unit of verse rhythm.

clue.text: Very big chap who went down to a stone

definitions.text: Very big chap who went down to a stone

parts.words: Very big chap who went down to a stone
parts.note: the biblical giant felled by David's slingshot pebble

explanation.surface: A large man lost weight down to a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went down to a stone' looks like dieting (a stone is 14 lb in Britain), but means falling to a slingshot stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine giant killed by David with a sling and stone.

clue.text: Egghead organised space flight

parts.note: the head, first letter, of egg is E

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An intellectual planned a space mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual; read it as the head of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight from danger is a getaway.

clue.text: King leaves to shorten meeting

indicators.note: the king leaves, so his letter departs from the word

parts.note: to contract is to shorten
R, for rex, is king

explanation.surface: A king leaves early to cut a meeting short.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming into contact with someone is meeting them.

clue.text: Loss in fuel is enormous

indicators.note: the loss goes inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel

explanation.surface: Wasted fuel amounts to a huge cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous and gigantic are synonyms for something very large.

clue.text: Book to read in bed?

parts.note: a yearly children's book read under the covers, or a plant living one season in a flower bed

explanation.surface: A book suitable for bedtime reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed: a plant that lives a single year grows there, and the same word is a yearly book.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearbook of comics, and a plant completing its life in one year, share this name.

clue.text: Impressive stamp edged with gold — the last word in France

indicators.note: the stamp is bordered on each side by the gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a stamp that makes an impression

explanation.surface: A gold-edged stamp of distinction, the final word in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell, literally to God, is the last thing said on parting.

clue.text: Bill and Ted executed

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two men named Bill and Ted were put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a plan or a part is to carry it out, to perform it.

clue.text: It's plain frozen

parts.note: plain is a level treeless expanse, and this one is frozen arctic ground

explanation.surface: Someone simply states that it is frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' reads as simply; it is a flat expanse of land.
explanation.definitionFit: The treeless arctic plain with permanently frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Adventurous girl embraces worker in Spanish port

indicators.note: the girl embraces, wraps around, the worker

parts.note: Alice has adventures in Wonderland
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A daring girl hugs a labourer in a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean seaport on Spain's Costa Blanca.

clue.text: You might say it when offering a gift or present

definitions.text: You might say it when offering a gift
definitions.meaning: said when handing something over, as in take this
in attendance, as in a roll call reply

explanation.surface: What someone says when handing over a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Said when handing something over, and meaning in attendance, as at a roll call.

clue.text: He used tax form that's expired

indicators.note: to form the letters is to shape them into something new

explanation.surface: A man filled in his tax form after the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like a tax form; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Expired can mean used up or spent, which matches being completely drained.
